Quebec Town Faces Uncertain Future as Trade War Idles Essential Paper Mill

01 Nov 2026, 10:48 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

Economic Disruption in Témiscaming

The town of Témiscaming, Quebec, is facing a potential economic collapse following the indefinite "economic shutdown" of its primary employer, a century-old paper mill. Owned by the American firm RYAM, the facility ceased operations in early October, impacting approximately 360 employees. The closure is directly linked to recent trade tensions between Canada and the United States, which saw the US impose 50% tariffs on various Canadian goods, including pulp and paper products.

Local Impact and Survival Strategies

Residents describe the mill as the town's economic anchor. Its closure has triggered several immediate concerns:

  • Real Estate Decline: Property values have reportedly fallen as residents fear the area could become a "ghost town."
  • Service Sustainability: Local fears extend to the viability of essential services, including grocery stores and the regional hospital.
  • Industry Ripple Effects: Local contractors serving the forestry supply chain have already begun implementing staff layoffs.

A History of Resistance

Facing similar existential threats in 1973, local workers and managers successfully orchestrated a buyout of the mill, transforming it into the international company Tembec. Current workers and union leaders are attempting to mobilize a new coalition to purchase the plant from RYAM, though they contend that substantial government intervention—such as tariff relief or financial aid—is required to make the venture viable.

Government Stance and Potential Remedies

While the federal government, led by Prime Minister Mark Carney, has provided significant financial support to Ontario's steel and auto sectors, local residents and regional representatives have expressed frustration over what they characterize as insufficient support for the forestry industry.

  • Government Response: A spokesperson for Industry Minister Mélanie Joly stated that $400 million has been allocated to support rural forestry sectors, with further programs launched to assist businesses in pivoting away from US-dependent markets.
  • Requested Action: Local officials, including Mayor Alain Gauthier, have called for reciprocal trade measures against US goods to pressure the US administration into easing existing duties.

As winter approaches, residents express urgency; prolonged idle time in sub-zero temperatures risks freezing and damaging plant equipment, which could complicate any future efforts to resume operations. Negotiations regarding a potential sale of the plant remain unconfirmed by RYAM.
